trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Roughly matched the market: +9.55% total return vs +14.41% for the index, +2.96pp residual after beta, -10.0% max drawdown, 0.15% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at +9.55% versus the S&P 500's +14.41% - effectively in line with simply holding the index.
The reversal premium this participant is built to harvest was live (+19.00% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
The momentum premium went against the declared exposure (+4.98% for a -0.5 loading) yet the account still returned +9.55% - the result was driven by something other than this factor.
Of the +9.55% total, about +6.59pp is explained by carrying beta 0.46 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.17); the residual +2.96pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
META contributed +3,152 USD (33% of net P&L) across 5 closed trades; GOOGL was the biggest drag at -3,467 USD.
Execution cost 152 USD (0.15% of starting capital, 0.7 bp per fill, 0.7 bp of the 2,134,136 USD traded). 73% of that was spread/depth/impact and 27% was explicit fees and rebates.
47 closed round trips, 70.2% winners, profit factor 1.44, average winner +948 vs average loser -1,556 USD, median holding 10 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 251 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 2563 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: NVDA long 2026-03-13 to 2026-03-27, -5,356 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -9.97% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-03-30, never recovered. Average gross exposure 32% of starting capital, peak leverage 1.78x.
Daily returns were +0.50 skewed with excess kurtosis +10.25; historical 95% VaR -1.22%/day with CVaR -2.26%/day. Worst single session -4.82%, best +5.47%.

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.
None of the failure modes declared in the strategy spec fired in this window.

Declared failure mode(s) this run CANNOT test, because no measurable condition matches their wording (they are neither confirmed nor ruled out): Catching a falling knife: a genuine fundamental break keeps falling; The 2-sigma filter fires most often exactly when volatility is rising; Exits are limit orders at the mean, so the best days can fail to fill.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 75.5pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @MeanRev_Z2Sigma (Mean Rev Z2) ran the "short-term reversal" archetype. Declared thesis: Liquidity provision is paid for. A large-cap that trades two standard deviations below its own 20-session mean in a single session has usually been hit by transient order flow, and it snaps back within days. Entry: Compute the z-score of yesterday's close against its 20-session mean; Buy names with z <= -2.0; Rank by most negative z, take up to 6 names; Skip names whose quoted spread exceeds 50 bp. Exit: Exit when z returns to >= -0.25 (back at the mean); Exit unconditionally after 10 sessions. Sizing: equal 30% of equity per name = up to 180% gross. Leverage: up to 1.8x gross. Cadence: daily, horizon 1-10 sessions. Aggression 4/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Buys the panic and is paid the liquidity premium, with turnover high enough to compound the edge.
